result:
I graded `submissions/s2.json` for quiz 0001 and wrote `grades/0001-s2.json`. Three items are correct, two are partial and one is wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | correct | The model only writes a tool request. This is better than your first attempt, where you chose `a`. |
| q3 | wrong (M6) | You let the agent run longer. A looping agent needs a stopping condition, such as a step limit. |
| q4 | partial (M4) | Your number, 4, is right. But the model does not run the tools. The program runs them. |
| q5 | correct | You gave both parts: the result goes back as the next input, and the model uses it to decide what to do next. |
| q6 | partial | The name is only part of it. The model also reads each tool's description and parameters. |

The grade-reviewer asked for two changes, and I made both. I shortened the summary to one focus and one next step. I also reworded the q6 feedback so it explains why a name alone can mislead. I kept the q4 verdict as partial with M4, as the reviewer advised. Your number is right, but your reason is wrong.

I also wrote learning record `0003-who-runs-the-tools-and-when-to-stop.md` and updated `NOTES.md`. `submissions/s1.json` is still not graded.

**Next step:** Trace the laser-cutter request on paper again. Mark each model call and each tool run, and mark who does each one.
